Dear Kristin and Ed,
Thank you for taking time out to meet with us this week.
It was a pleasure learning about the important work USAID is doing to support Afghans at this critical time
and also share with you some of our efforts around safety, girls education, women's economic resilience
and the distribution of humanitarian aid.
Also, thank you for offering to connect us with the right folks at the World Bank, ADB and the NSC. 1 am
sharing below an overview of our work in Atghanistan and my bio in case you would like to share it with the
relevant POCs at these organisations. I could extend my stay till Tuesday next week if we think an in-persor
meeting would be more fruitful. In case that's too ambitious a timeline, we can certainly plan for virtual calls
at a later date.
I hope this is the beginning of many fruitful conversations.
Warm regards,

Overview of Meta's work in Afghanistan-Meta's efforts in Afghanistan pre-date the August 15th crisis of
last year. However, over the last year we have increased our commitment to our community of users in
Afghanistan in light of the evolving risk landscape in the country. Below is a broad overview of some of our
key workstreams in Afghanistan:
1. On-platform Integrity: This pillar focuseson removing harmful content and behaviour from our
platforms. We work with local and international experts to continuously improve our policies and
proactive and reactive enforcement as well as monitor new trends in user behaviour that could
adversely impact the voice and safety of our community of users.
1. We have a specialized regional team of Afghans monitoring user and content trends in
Afghanistan and diaspora; a team of over 300 global safety experts to ensure that we are
staying on top of emerging risks, and a network of local, diaspora and international CSOs
serving as Trusted Partners and providing insights on emerging risks on the ground. We use
these insights to continuously improve our overall integrity landscape.
1. Programs - This pillar builds on our integrity efforts by working in partnership with local and
international government and non-governmental organizations in the country and diaspora on joint
areas of priorities such as girls education, women's safety and economic resiliency, digital literacy,
mental health, and journalist safety and capacity building. We consult with Afghans within the country
and diaspora on these themes and how our programs could effectively support them. Working with
the Alliance of AWER and the US-Afghan Consultative Mechanisms are some examples of this work.
2. Products and Tools - This pillar focuses on utilizing existing tools or innovating new ones to tackle
specific issues in Afghanistan or globally. We recognise the unique challenges in Afghanistan and are
constantly thinking about how our platforms could scale solutions that help our community. Some
examples of this include:
1. During the August 15th crisis, we launched 'locked profile' and 'disappearing messages'
and sent targeted messages to users in Dari and Pashto to inform them of these
resources and how to enable them.
2. We have launched a 'Community Help Centre' to help INGOs and local CSOs coordinate
humanitarian relief efforts and scale them to the most remote parts of Afghanistan
through our platforms. We are working to build these organizations' capacity so they can
maximize their use of this tool.
Bio
Ayesha Hashem is part of Meta's APAC Public Policy Emerging Markets team where she leads Public
Policy for Afghanistan and Nepal. Ayesha has been with Meta for almost four years, initially working on
global content policy issues such as civic integrity, child safety, and health misinformation before
transitioning to the Public Policy role last year. Ayesha led Meta's response to the August 15th crisis in
Afghanistan and has since been engaging with civil society partners in Afghanistan and the diaspora, IGOs
and INGOs, think tanks, academics, journalists, and activists working in or on Afghanistan around topics of
terrorism, safety and economic resilience of women and minority groups, digital literacy, and the ongoing
humanitarian crisis.

Hi Maria,
I hope you're well. I wanted to share that Ayesha Hashem, our head of Public Policy for
Afghanistan (biography below), will be in Washington, D.C. next week, September 26 - 30.
If your schedule permits, we'd like to request a meeting to brief you on Meta's Afghanistan
workstreams and discuss key policy issues, including the ongoing situation on the ground
and the safety of vulnerable members of the Afghan community. We'd be happy to host this
meeting in-person at our Meta office as well. Many thanks for your consideration. Please
let us know if there is a convenient time for you next week and with whom we should be in
touch regarding logistics. Copying Felicia to coordinate schedules. Thank you.
Ayesha Hashem
